events.title: George Washington is born in Virginia
events.description: The future first President of the United States was born at his family's plantation on Popes Creek in Westmoreland County, Virginia. He grew up to command the Continental Army and preside over the Constitutional Convention.
events.significance: Washington became the central figure of the American founding. His birthday was long celebrated as a national holiday, and it is now commemorated as Presidents' Day.

events.title: French troops land at Fishguard, Wales
events.description: About 1,200 French soldiers landed near Fishguard in Pembrokeshire. They were poorly disciplined, and local militia and civilians confronted them. The French surrendered within days.
events.significance: It is generally regarded as the last invasion of mainland Britain. It showed how far French revolutionary ambitions reached during the wars of the 1790s.

events.title: The 'Miracle on Ice'
events.description: At the Winter Olympics in Lake Placid, New York, a team of American amateur and collegiate players beat the heavily favored Soviet Union in ice hockey.
events.significance: The upset came at a tense point in the Cold War. It became one of the most celebrated moments in American sports history and a symbol of national pride.

events.title: Andy Warhol dies in New York City
events.description: The pop art pioneer died at age 58 from complications after routine gallbladder surgery.
events.significance: Warhol's work blurred the line between fine art, advertising and celebrity culture. His influence on contemporary art and popular culture endures.
